Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

race noun

a people of common descent

also races, racial, race relations, racism, racist, racial discrimination, ethnic group, of mixed race, nation

classical

Cic. Off. 1.53: ejusdem gentis, nātiōnis, linguae (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 205

gēns, gentis f.

noun, third declension

race, people, nation

Properly a Roman clan; in a wider sense a race or people, beside nātiō and populus. “Racial” is the genitive: gentis, generis (“of race”).

Other words

  • genus, generis n. — race, stock, descent

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.286: malō genere nātus (Lewis & Short); Traupman 368

    Birth and descent, the stock a person comes from; also “kind, sort” in general. genus hūmānum is the human race (see human).

  • stirps, stirpis f. — stock, lineage

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · M-O s.v. race (classification of humans; Egger)

    Literally the stock of a plant, then a family line. Morgan–Owens gives it, after Egger, for race as a classification of people.

  • odium in aliēnigenās — racism, hatred of foreigners

    phrase · also used · modern · M-O s.v. racism

    aliēnigena is classical (Cic., Liv.), one born abroad; Morgan–Owens offers this, or invidia in aliēnigenās, for racial prejudice.

Examples

  • propior est ejusdem gentis, nātiōnis, linguae, quā maximē hominēs conjunguntur

    closer is the bond of the same race, nation and language, by which people are most closely joinedCic. Off. 1.53 (Lewis & Short)

See also human, minority, foreign, state.
